# Security Policy

If you think you have identified a security issue with a Pydantic project, **do not open a public issue**.

To responsibly report a security issue, please navigate to the "Security" tab for the repo, and click "Report a vulnerability".

![Screenshot of repo security tab showing "Report a vulnerability" button](https://github.com/pydantic/.github/raw/main/assets/github_report_vulnerability.png)

Be sure to include as much detail as necessary in your report. As with reporting normal issues, a minimal reproducible example will help the maintainers address the issue faster.

Thank you.

name: Security vulnerability report
description: Report a vulnerability with a realistic threat model and a minimal reproduction.
body:
  - type: markdown
    attributes:
      value: |
        Thank you for reporting privately. Explain how an attacker can cause real harm in normal usage.
        Run reproductions only in a local, isolated environment you control. Do not include credentials or private data.

  - type: textarea
    id: summary
    attributes:
      label: Summary
      description: Describe the vulnerability, its cause, and the security property it violates. Include a CWE if known.
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: textarea
    id: affected_versions
    attributes:
      label: Affected package and environment
      description: |
        List the package name, exact version you tested, and other affected versions if known.
        Include your runtime, operating system, and relevant dependency versions.
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: textarea
    id: threat_model
    attributes:
      label: Threat model
      description: |
        What can the attacker control? What authentication, privileges, or access do they need?
        Identify the victim and the trust boundary crossed. Do the prerequisites already let the attacker cause the claimed harm?
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: textarea
    id: details
    attributes:
      label: Real-world usage and vulnerable behavior
      description: |
        Describe a realistic application configuration and input that trigger the issue within documented preconditions.
        Link relevant code, documentation, or specifications. Explain why this is not standard behavior or an explicitly documented limitation.
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: textarea
    id: proof_of_concept
    attributes:
      label: Minimal reproducible example
      description: |
        Provide complete, self-contained code or raw requests, ideally under 40 lines, plus exact setup and run commands.
        Pin the tested package version. Avoid servers, CLIs, and test frameworks unless the issue requires them.
        Include observed output and an assertion, measurement, or other evidence of exploitation, not just unexpected behavior.
        Describe any network requests, file writes, shell commands, or other side effects before the code.
        Include a comparison with a fixed version if available.
    validations:
      required: true
      min_length: 150

  - type: textarea
    id: impact
    attributes:
      label: Security impact
      description: |
        Explain the concrete harm to the victim and how it follows from the attacker's stated capabilities.
        For denial of service, include timings or resource measurements under realistic workloads and deployment limits.
        Judge the technical behavior directly. An existing GHSA or CVE identifier alone does not establish impact.
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: textarea
    id: remediation
    attributes:
      label: Suggested remediation or workaround
      description: |
        If you have a proposal, describe it and any compatibility or performance costs.
        Explain why those costs are proportionate to the realistic impact.
    validations:
      required: false
